problems.title: Theatre Square (Codeforces 1A)
problems.description: Cover an n × m square with a × a flagstones. Round up each side with integer division, and note the answer can reach 10¹⁸: it needs long long. Difficulty 1000.

problems.title: Even Odds (Codeforces 318A)
problems.description: Find the k-th number when all odd numbers up to n come before the even ones. n is up to 10¹², so int overflows; a small formula avoids building the list. Difficulty 900.

problems.title: Drinks (Codeforces 200B)
problems.description: Mix equal amounts of drinks and print the orange-juice percentage. Practises double division (not integer division) and printing decimals. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Word (Codeforces 59A)
problems.description: Turn a word all-uppercase or all-lowercase, whichever needs fewer changes. Practises counting and converting letter case with chars. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Petya and Strings (Codeforces 112A)
problems.description: Compare two words alphabetically, ignoring upper and lower case. Practises tolower and string comparison. Difficulty 800.

exercises.title: A Very Big Sum (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Add up numbers that are each up to 10¹⁰. The total doesn't fit in int: use long long.

exercises.title: Missing Number (CSES)
exercises.description: All numbers 1…n are given except one; find it. The sum 1 + 2 + … + n can exceed int, so use long long.

exercises.title: Plus One (LeetCode 66)
exercises.description: Add one to a number given digit by digit. It can have up to 100 digits, more than any integer type holds, so work on the digits and carry.

exercises.title: CamelCase (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Count the words in a camelCase string by counting uppercase letters. Practises char checks like std::isupper.

exercises.title: Repetitions (CSES)
exercises.description: Find the longest run of the same letter in a DNA string of up to 10⁶ characters. Practises walking through a std::string.

exercises.title: To Lower Case (LeetCode 709)
exercises.description: Convert a string to lowercase yourself, using char arithmetic ('A' + 32 = 'a') instead of a library call.

challenges.title: Data Types: Numbers
challenges.description: Pick the right number type. Start with the exercises (big sums and digit-by-digit numbers), then the Codeforces problems: Drinks (doubles), Even Odds and Theatre Square (long long and rounding up).

challenges.title: Data Types: Characters & Strings
challenges.description: Work with chars and text. Do the three exercises first (uppercase checks, runs of letters, char arithmetic), then Word and Petya and Strings on Codeforces.

quizzes.title: Data Types in C++
quizzes.description: Five questions on integer ranges, division, floating point and chars. Answers are revealed after you submit.

questions.question: About how large can a value in a (32-bit) int get?
With int a = 7 and int b = 2, what is a / b?
Why can 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 be false for doubles?
answers: Most decimal fractions can't be stored exactly, so tiny rounding errors appear
== doesn't work on doubles at all
doubles only keep two decimal places

questions.question: You read up to 10⁶ numbers, each up to 10⁹, and need their sum. Which type should the sum be?
What is the value of '7' - '0' in C++?

lessons.title: Data Types in C++
lessons.description:
Choosing the right type, and the bugs the wrong one causes: integer ranges and overflow, long long and unsigned, integer division, floating-point precision, char and ASCII maths, conversions, auto and std::string.

Read the lesson and the links. Then try the "Data Types: Numbers" and "Data Types: Characters & Strings" challenges under Practice and the "Data Types in C++" quiz.
